title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (vFinal)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the Unified Inference product overview, the final PRD and requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the vFinal delivery. It is intended for product managers, engineering, go-to-market, and executive stakeholders.

Goal:
- Provide a single source of truth for what we are shipping under the "Unified Inference" initiative.
- Align engineering and GTM on scope, success metrics, pricing, and rollout plan.

Executive summary:
- Unified Inference delivers a single developer experience and control plane for Redwood-hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private deployments.
- Key customer problems addressed: unpredictable latency/cost, model sprawl across environments, and operational complexity when scaling LLM-powered features.
- vFinal scope focuses on (1) model routing & cost-aware fallbacks, (2) rollout and canary tooling, (3) improved pricing tiers and packaging for Dedicated & Private, and (4) observability improvements tied to cost and quality.

Product requirements (PRD):
1) Core user stories:
   1. As an engineer, I can pin a model version and define rollout policies (canary, A/B, percentage-based) that apply consistently across Hosted, Dedicated and Private.
   2. As an SRE, I can set routing policies that prioritize latency or cost and configure automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.
   3. As a product owner, I can view token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns in the Console and export monthly cost reports.
   4. As a security admin, I can enable Private deployment controls (VPC, KMS integration, audit logs) with the same control plane UX.

2) Functional requirements (must-have):
   - API: single REST/SDK surface for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking; new endpoints for rollout management (PATCH /v1/rollouts).
   - Rollouts: canary, A/B, fixed-percentage, time-based rollouts; rollback and automatic fallback policies.
   - Routing: policy-based routing by latency/cost/region; deterministic fallback chains; model variant catalog and compatibility metadata.
   - Observability: per-route token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, error budget burn rate, request traces linked to model versions.
   - Billing: usage aggregation across deployment modes and customer-configurable cost centers/tags.

3) Non-functional requirements (SLOs & constraints):
   - Latency SLOs: p95 single-turn text generation <= 250ms for standard models on Dedicated with reserved capacity; host-mode p95 depends on plan.
   - Availability: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated customers with monthly SLA.
   - Security: support KMS for Private keys, RBAC for rollout controls, and audit logging retention configurable to 365 days.

4) Acceptance criteria:
   - End-to-end rollout: create a canary rollout, verify traffic split, observe metrics in Console, and execute rollback without request loss.
   - Routing: when a primary model is saturated, traffic is automatically routed to configured fallback and results meet compatibility metadata constraints.
   - Billing: exported monthly report matches internal usage counters within 1% variance.

Design specs (high level):
- Architecture:
  - Control plane: single control API (hosted) that stores rollout configs, model catalog, and routing policies. For Private deployments, control plane runs in customer VPC or via private-control-plane option.
  - Data plane: region-aware inference clusters (hosted/dedicated/private) with a lightweight routing proxy that applies policies and communicates to the serving runtime.
  - Model catalog metadata: model_id, variant_id, compatibility vector (max_seq, tokenizer, kv-cache compatible), cost_score (tokens/sec normalized), latency_profile.

- APIs and data models (examples):
  - Rollout spec (fields): rollout_id, model_candidates (list), strategy (canary/ab-test/percentage), start_time, end_time, health_checks (p95_latency_threshold, error_rate_threshold).
  - Routing policy (fields): policy_id, priority (latency|cost|region), fallback_chain (ordered model_variant_ids).

- UI/Console flows:
  - Rollout creation wizard with preview traffic distribution, quick health threshold presets, and audit trail.
  - Per-route dashboard with latency, cost, tokens, error rate, and ability to force-traffic or initiate rollback.

Roadmap & themes (quarterly milestones):
- Q2 2026: foundational rollout APIs, model catalog metadata, and basic routing policies (latency priority).
- Q3 2026: canary/A-B rollouts, fallback chains, Console rollout UI, and initial Dedicated packaging changes.
- Q4 2026: cost-aware routing, per-route cost dashboards, and first Dedicated SLA.
- Q1 2027: Private deployment control-plane options, KMS integration, and advanced rollout health checks.
- Q2 2027: unified pricing tiers and packaging launch (see pricing section), improved autoscaling for Dedicated.
- Q3 2027: mature observability (traces + quality monitoring), model quantization recommendations integrated into Optimize.

Pricing & packaging notes (summary):
- Hosted API: continued usage-based pricing (per-token generation and embedding units) with new tiered plans (developer, scale, enterprise) that add throughput caps, retention, and SLAs.
- Dedicated: move to committed monthly/annual pricing with 3 standard packages (Small, Medium, Large) defined by vGPU count, baseline throughput, and optional burst. Pricing is a combination of reserved capacity + overage per token.
- Private: license + annual support fee. Pricing tiers vary by node count and optional on-prem support. Additional charges for compliance add-ons (SOC2 + support retention).
- Price experiment guardrails:
  - Launch baseline MSRP for Small/Medium/Large with 10% introductory discounts for committed 12-months.
  - Metering model: token-based with separate flat infra fee for Dedicated and Private.

Packaging & go-to-market notes:
- Offer a "Dedicated Starter" pack for mid-market teams (3-month trial, reduced onboarding).
- GTM bundles: product + Optimize credits for first-year customers to encourage cost/perf tuning.
- Updated sales collaterals include per-use case TCO examples and latency/cost benchmarks for common workloads (chat, semantic search, embeddings).

Rollout plan & operational readiness:
1. Staged rollout: internal dogfood -> select beta customers (5 customers, mix of startups and enterprises) -> general availability.
2. Pre-launch runbook: define on-call rotation, escalation path, rollback playbook, and capacity pre-warm checklist.
3. Metrics to monitor during rollout: traffic distribution correctness, p95 latency by route/model, fallback frequency, cost delta vs baseline, and error budget burn.

Release notes (vFinal):
- New: unified rollout APIs (canary/A-B/percentage), Console rollout wizard, and audit trail.
- New: policy-based routing with deterministic fallback chains and cost-aware routing engine.
- Improved: per-route cost and latency dashboards; monthly exportable billing reports.
- Improved: Dedicated packaging with SLA definitions and autoscaling improvements.
- Security: KMS support for Private (beta), RBAC controls for rollout management, and extended audit log retention settings.
- Known limitations: Private control-plane deployment in air-gapped environments requires on-prem control-plane package (GA planned Q3 2027). Some legacy model variants need manual compatibility tagging for fallback.

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: inaccurate cost attribution across hybrid deployments. Mitigation: implement reconciliation job and double-check monthly exports during beta; require tagging enforcement.
- Risk: rollout-induced regressions. Mitigation: default conservative health thresholds, automatic rollbacks, and canary first for high-risk routes.

Ownership & next steps:
- Product lead: Avery Chen (owner).
- Engineering leads: Ravi Patel (control plane & rollout), Morgan Lee (serving runtime integration), Sofia Ramirez (Console/observability).
- QA & Evals: coordinate with Applied ML & Evals team for quality regressions tied to rollout prompts.
- Next steps: finalize pricing SKU sheet, publish beta sign-up, and schedule 4-week GA readiness review on 2027-06-01.

Appendices:
- Appendix A: Example rollout CLI usage:
  - redwood rollout create --name chat-canary --model m-gpt-std:2027-02 --strategy canary --percent 5 --health-check p95<250ms

- Appendix B: Minimal rollout JSON (example):
  {
    "rollout_id": "r-1234",
    "strategy": "canary",
    "candidates": ["m-gpt-std:2027-02", "m-gpt-quant:2027-02"],
    "percent": 5
  }
